<!-- go-guitar-pro-capability-work:whammy -->

Use the exact curve-position contract from #60 for GPIF and binary whammy points without losing authored control-role order.

**Type:** implementation. **Priority:** P1. **Capability:** `whammy`.
**Formats:** gp3, gp4, gp5, gp6, gp7, gp8. **Stages to assess:** import, model, export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve a non-grid offset such as 35% and a fractional percentage such as 35.5 through public import/edit/export and retaining pinned-consumer assertions.
- [ ] Exercise origin, two middle offsets sharing one value, and destination; preserve control order and the exact-offset/legacy Position authority established by #60.
- [ ] Keep interior-hold and unequal-rate tests, with narrow loss reports for consumer gesture interpretation or unrepresentable shapes. Passing a rounded self-round-trip is insufficient.
- [ ] Cover valid nonmonotonic standard tuples under #62 where applicable, and retain explicit reports for style/summary metadata, per-point vibrato, excess controls and incompatible middle heights.

Any public API change must expose the authored value with a documented edit/reconciliation contract. Add a non-default public API regression and independent pinned-consumer export evidence. Preserve compatibility or explicitly document the change.

## Scope boundaries

- No new style-token mapping or broad normalization waiver. Extend the common precision contract rather than inventing a competing whammy scale.

## Reproduction and evidence

Preserve a non-grid offset such as 35% and a fractional percentage such as 35.5 through public import/edit/export and retaining pinned-consumer assertions. See the linked investigation decision and review receipt for the confirmed baseline.

Use the named fixtures and non-default cases above. The linked investigation and review distinguish reproduced failures from source-backed implementation gaps.

- AlphaTab [Beat.whammyStyle](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Beat.ts#L275)
- AlphaTab [Beat.isContinuedWhammy](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Beat.ts#L463)
- AlphaTab [Beat.whammyBarType](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Beat.ts#L468)
- AlphaTab [Beat.whammyBarPoints](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Beat.ts#L475)
- Repository [gpif_effects.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1/gpif_effects.go)
- Repository [gp8_effects.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1/gp8_effects.go)
- field: `BeatEffects.TremoloBar`. Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.
- test: `TestConformanceCurvePreservation`. Existing scoped evidence; not proof of all AlphaTab variants.
- investigation-review: `https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/issues/72#issuecomment-5624495922`. implementation-ready: Whammy uses the same 0..12 rounding and writer scale as bends; its precision work is concrete after the shared representation and role-aware validation changes.

Oracle: AlphaTab 1.8.4, revision `022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d`. Audit baseline: `30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1`.

## Dependencies and coordination

- Complete [#60](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/issues/60): Preserve exact authored bend offsets.
- Complete [#62](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/issues/62): Preserve GPIF bend control roles with nonmonotonic offsets.

Before claiming, refresh issue state and check `ready_work` and `work_conflicts`. Mark the work item `in_progress` with an owner. Source pointers are starting points; shared-file overlap is advisory and not an exhaustive conflict map.

## Verification and inventory update

- Follow `AGENTS.md`, `docs/semantic-model.md`, and `conformance/README.md` for semantic changes. Add domain-named tests and update `conformance/feature-ledger.json`.
- Run `./conformance/check.sh` and `prek run --all-files` for semantic changes. Rerun the capability probe before claiming a gap is resolved.
- Update the [canonical work item](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/main/conformance/capabilities/work-items/whammy.json) with the resolution, verified commit, command results, and evidence. Update the scoped catalog assessment separately; tests passing or issue closure never promote it automatically.
- Run `python3 conformance/capabilities/manage.py refresh` and commit the JSON, database, and generated reports together.
- Review every acceptance criterion against the exact final commit and completed prerequisites before closing. Record residual limits and open follow-up issues.

[Agent workflow](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/main/conformance/capabilities/README.md) · [Full backlog](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/main/conformance/capabilities/BACKLOG.md)

<!-- capability-investigation-review-2026-09-10 -->

## Review outcome

**implementation-ready** — Whammy uses the same 0..12 rounding and writer scale as bends; its precision work is concrete after the shared representation and role-aware validation changes.

Reviewed against `f5a5ee962d086c369d2e523ba2de98ca1ddd481b` and pinned AlphaTab `022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d`. The original [investigation evidence](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/issues/72#issuecomment-5624495922) remains part of this ticket.

The implementation acceptance checklist above replaces the earlier investigation deliverable. Scope exclusions remain explicit; this conversion does not mark the capability supported.

Reviewed starting points: [effects.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/f5a5ee962d086c369d2e523ba2de98ca1ddd481b/effects.go), [gpif_effects.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/f5a5ee962d086c369d2e523ba2de98ca1ddd481b/gpif_effects.go), [gp8_effects.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/f5a5ee962d086c369d2e523ba2de98ca1ddd481b/gp8_effects.go), [conformance_curves_test.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/f5a5ee962d086c369d2e523ba2de98ca1ddd481b/conformance_curves_test.go).

[Full review](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/main/conformance/capabilities/INVESTIGATION-REVIEW.md)

comments.body:
## Investigation complete — implementation-ready

**Disposition: dependency on #60 for precision; remaining style losses are target limits.**

GPIF Whammy uses the same standard curve shape as bends: origin, two middle offsets sharing one middle value, and destination. Pinned AlphaTab writes 2–4 points and derives whammy type/style from the resulting curve. There is no authored style token or per-point vibrato in this record. Existing Go tests already cover an interior hold and unequal-rate curve and report curves that cannot fit the shared-middle representation.

After #60 establishes exact offset precision, apply the same scale to whammy points and preserve point order. Continue reporting explicit public style, per-point vibrato, more than four points, or incompatible middle values as target limits. Do not invent a separate style mapping unless a real GP3–GP8 wire field is found. This issue can become an implementation task only for the precision dependency; the rest is an accepted strict-policy boundary.

Reviewed: [Go source](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/tree/e6020364ab58ef71c2710d3b138d1d4c48e9ad81), [pinned AlphaTab](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/tree/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d). <!-- investigation-decision-ready-2026-09-10 -->

## Investigation complete — implementation-ready

**Disposition: implementation follow-up for curve precision; explicit target limits for style metadata.**

Evidence at the pinned AlphaTab revision shows that GPIF bend offsets use 0..100 on the wire and AlphaTab retains them as 0..60. Values are quarter tones (wire value / 25). The Go model instead scales offset to 0..12, so authored offsets such as 35% are rounded and cannot round-trip exactly. GPIF's standard bend record has origin, two middle offsets sharing one middle value, and destination: 2–4 control points. It has no authored bend-kind/style field and no per-point vibrato field; AlphaTab derives style from the curve.

**Next-step contract:** widen or replace the public bend-position scale so GPIF can retain 0..60 (or the exact wire ratio), update binary/GPIF conversions and matrix assertions, and preserve point order. Keep curves outside the 2–4/shared-middle shape, explicit public 'BendType', and per-point vibrato as reported target limits. AlphaTab itself truncates non-quarter-tone wire values, so those need a separate oracle if exact support is proposed.

## Investigation complete — implementation-ready

**Disposition: exporter validation bug; create a bounded implementation follow-up.**

The identical GP7/GP8 fixture 'testdata/gp7/canon-audio-track.gp' (SHA-256 'dd50673…') parses in Go and pinned AlphaTab, but Go export rejects three curves because the destination offset (35) follows middle offsets (50). This is not a reason to sort the points: sorting changes origin/middle/destination roles and the curve. The follow-up should preserve the standard GPIF control tuple exactly and relax the generic monotonic invariant at the GPIF boundary (or represent the control roles explicitly). It must reproduce the wire fields, pass Go reparse and pinned AlphaTab, and retain rejection for shapes that cannot be assigned valid GPIF roles.
